title: Check fixed-bank pulse relations after the 679-owner BIT specialization
body:
The #7912 specialization creates no new same-bank pulse relation in the surviving graph. The four changed adjoint banks keep full rank and every surviving reverse pulse is unchanged.

## Scope and source

Pins the actual #7912 recompilation, the surviving owner and paid rosters, and original bank memberships. This covers relations in its fixed graph. The complete source comparator is #7830 at `87fbf4f7b35b0f18ab12b5767775a9a424cf0b15`. The archive identifies additional inputs by exact commit, path and hash. Base `e54523517d0f03e58352e647c403a5af3e525a57`; P104 toolkit #7852 `41beda1d6435760dc99e38bd7e65f36798aad212`.

## Reproduction

Extract `research/p104-bit679-postspecialization-cut/replay.tar.gz` into an empty directory. Check its inner checksum manifest. `python3 -IB verify.py` cold replay reproduced both 679- and 680-owner operators, paired signed zero, and the independent rank and subset checks. The archive preserves the verification evidence and controls. This is an offline research archive; hosted package execution is separate.

## Open next questions

A cascade would need a different first edit that introduces a usable relation or a changed bank.

Clear1nsight prepared this result with substantial OpenAI Codex assistance. Credit DreamingOfClouds for the P104 toolkit and the predecessor authors identified in the archive. Related results: [P104 campaign board](https://github.com/CrocSwap/integer-mult-bounds/discussions/7111#discussioncomment-19789228).
